- Absence of reported fever, lymphadenopathy, or systemic symptoms — reduces likelihood of DRESS or systemic infection.  
- Biopsy confirms subepidermal blistering with autoimmune basement membrane targeting — excludes intraepidermal disorders (e.g., pemphigus, spongiotic dermatitis) and non-immune causes.

- Specific names, classes, and start dates of the four new medications — critical to identify known BP-inducing agents (e.g., furosemide, NSAIDs, penicillamine, DPP-4 inhibitors, PD-1 inhibitors).  
- Anti-BP180 (BPAG2) and anti-BP230 antibody titers — gold-standard serologic confirmation of BP; absence would challenge the diagnosis.  
- Salt-split skin immunofluorescence or anti-type VII collagen (COL7) antibodies — needed to definitively exclude epidermolysis bullosa acquisita.  
- Serum IgE level — elevated IgE supports BP (vs. EBA or linear IgA), but not yet obtained.
